title: Bound the whole viscous mixed response uniformly in amplitude
statement: For the SAME mixed pair, S_t+alpha(t)sin(kappa x2)partial1 S=nu Delta S,S0=cos(kappa x1), and V=exp(-nu kappa^2t)e2 cos(kappa x1). The COMPLETE vertical quadratic coefficient solves W2_t+alpha sin(kappa x2)partial1 W2=nu Delta W2-V.grad S,W2(0)=0. Scalar dissipation gives2nu integral||grad S||2^2<=1/2,||V||infinity<=1, hence ||W2(t)||2<=sqrt(t/(4nu)) and ||W2(5T)||2<=sqrt(5T/(4nu)) for EVERY shear amplitude A. This controls the whole mixed coefficient, not merely its zero-streamwise projection, but not the full quadratic operator/higher iterates/general3D flow. The large inviscid resonance and the fixed-positive-viscosity bound have distinct hypotheses and are compatible.
